title: CP8/26 - Funded reinsurance
key_claim: The PRA proposes to recalibrate the counterparty default adjustment on funded reinsurance so that capital held against the average transaction rises to around 10% of underlying annuity liabilities from 2-4%, applying to arrangements entered from October 2026 with a savings provision for risks fully transferred on or before 30 September 2026 and implementation from 1 July 2027.
frame_summary: Argues that funded reinsurance receives materially more favourable capital treatment than economically similar direct investments, and that the retained risk which justifies intervention is the cedant's exposure if the arrangement is recaptured.
verbatim_quote: In aggregate, for an average FundedRe deal, the PRA expects total valuation and capital charges of around c.10% of the best estimate of the underlying annuity liabilities, after including the CDA, the SCR and the risk margin. This compares to the 2–4% previously noted in 2025 industry roundtable discussions.
verbatim_list: In recent years, about 15% of new BPA business has been ceded via funded reinsurance arrangements.

LIST 2025 tested the year-end 2024 impact of recapturing funded reinsurance exposures from just firms’ largest single counterparty. This covered £12.3 billion of liabilities – on average 4% of underlying annuity liabilities. A scenario where all firms recaptured exposures with their largest counterparty led to a reduction in SCR coverage ratios of 10 percentage points: a reduction in surplus capital of c.£3 billion.
The PRA proposes that the savings provision should apply to business where the risks covered are fully transferred on or before 30 September 2026.

In a scenario where there is no change in firms’ use of funded reinsurance, this could lead to additional initial new business capital requirements of c.£700 million per year across the market, reflecting the estimates in paragraphs 4.3 and 4.12. This compares to total UK BPA writer own funds of c£80 billion.
BPA business is estimated to be around a third of UK life insurers’ non-linked liabilities, ie c.£300 billion of c.£850 billion total non-linked life insurance technical provisions.
The PRA therefore expects the proposals to have a modest immediate impact on overall BPA pricing and volumes.
notes: Structural anchor: canonical primary source for the recapture-pricing framing. Outside the 90-day window (110 days) but within 6 months; consultation closed 31 July 2026. Quote confirmed by hand against the live CP8/26 page, paragraph 4.11, during the 17/08/2026 WebFetch: "In aggregate, for an average FundedRe deal, the PRA expects total valuation and capital charges of around c.10% of the best estimate of the underlying annuity liabilities, after including the CDA, the SCR and the risk margin. This compares to the 2–4% previously noted in 2025 industry roundtable discussions." Audit script 403s behind the sandbox proxy.

title: Preview of NAIC Committee and Task Force Activities for the 2026 Summer National Meeting
date_evidence:

key_claim: The NAIC's Financial Condition (E) Committee agenda for the August 2026 Summer National Meeting includes whether to change the reinsurance thresholds and requirements in the Disclosure of Material Transactions Model Act, and the International Insurance Relations (G) Committee agenda includes cross-border reinsurance.
frame_summary: Frames offshore life reinsurance as a live supervisory workstream requiring better disclosure and cross-border coordination rather than a settled arrangement, placing it on the agenda of two separate NAIC committees in the same cycle.

title: IAIS mid-year Global Insurance Market Report 2026
key_claim: Aggregate systemic risk scores of global insurance groups rose slightly at year-end 2025, with the largest increases in asset liquidation to generate excess cash and in interconnectedness between insurers, financial markets and the broader economy.
frame_summary: Argues that the global insurance sector is stable in aggregate but that its interconnectedness and forced-sale channels are the parts of the risk picture that have deteriorated, which is where supervisory attention should sit.
verbatim_list: Aggregate systemic risk scores of global insurance groups at year-end 2025 increased slightly compared to year-end 2024, with the largest increases recorded in asset liquidation to generate excess cash and interconnectedness between insurers, financial markets and the broader economy.
notes: Used for the interconnectedness framing, not for any number in the body.

title: Future of UK funded reinsurance in flux as capital charge raised
key_claim: Use of funded reinsurance by UK life insurers is expected to diminish following the PRA's proposals, and the change should favour reinsurers with higher financial strength ratings.
frame_summary: Argues that the PRA's move does not simply raise a cost but sorts the reinsurance market by counterparty credit quality, so the effect falls unevenly across reinsurers rather than uniformly across the market.
notes: Body text sits behind a registration wall; claim taken from the publicly rendered standfirst. No number in the article body is sourced here.

title: Bulk annuity market: Q3 2026 trustee update

key_claim: UK bulk annuity volumes in the first half of 2026 were below £10bn, lower than recent years, with XPS expecting around £35bn for the full year and pricing remaining strong on heightened insurer competition.
frame_summary: Argues that current UK buyout conditions are being set by insurer competition and scheme size rather than by regulatory change, so trustees should read pricing as a competitive outcome rather than a policy signal.

title: US regulators seek tighter rules for offshore life reinsurance
key_claim: The NAIC's Financial Condition (E) Committee has directed the Life Risk-Based Capital Working Group to develop a reinsurance recapture RBC factor for reserves ceded outside reciprocal jurisdictions, prioritised for year-end 2027, with Cayman's life and annuities sector holding about $101 billion at end-2025 against $23 billion in 2020.
frame_summary: Argues that the live regulatory question in US life reinsurance is jurisdictional equivalence rather than asset quality, and that capital requirements should distinguish between reciprocal and non-reciprocal domiciles.
verbatim_quote: A reinsurance recapture RBC factor to be applied to ceded reserves and modified coinsurance balances for all reinsurance located outside of reciprocal jurisdictions
verbatim_list: By the end of 2025, Cayman’s life and annuities sector held about $101 billion in total assets, up from $23 billion in 2020.
The Committee directs that these efforts be prioritised so that the changes are in place for year-end 2027.
notes: Reports the Houdek memo to the Life Risk-Based Capital (E) Working Group; the memo itself is not separately published online. Quote confirmed by hand against the live page, first bullet of the committee's two recommended changes, during the 17/08/2026 WebFetch: "A reinsurance recapture RBC factor to be applied to ceded reserves and modified coinsurance balances for all reinsurance located outside of reciprocal jurisdictions while of course considering an overcollateralising of the reserves..." Audit script 403s behind the sandbox proxy.

title: Bermuda captures 41% of ceded US life liabilities
key_claim: Alirt Insurance Research found that about $1.1 trillion of the $2.7 trillion in life and annuity liabilities ceded by US life insurers at year-end 2025 went to Bermudian reinsurers, 40.7 per cent of all ceded liabilities and 85 per cent of liabilities ceded outside the US.
frame_summary: Argues that offshore cession has become a core capital-management tool for US life insurers rather than a peripheral one, which is why reserve adequacy and counterparty risk now dominate the regulatory agenda.
verbatim_list: Bermuda captures 41% of ceded US life liabilities
About $1.1 trillion of the $2.7 trillion in life and annuity liabilities ceded by US life insurers as of year-end 2025, were ceded to Bermudian-based reinsurers, new Alirt research has reported.
This represented 40.7 per cent of all ceded liabilities and 85 per cent of liabilities ceded to non-US jurisdictions.
notes: Scale anchor for the size of the exposure the new capital factors would sit against.

title: Bermuda life reinsurers face scrutiny as US insurers pivot to new structured products
key_claim: The NAIC adopted revised risk-based capital factors for CLO investments on 23 June 2026, effective for year-end 2026 filings and covering approximately US$314 billion of exposure, but insurers had already shifted into structured products the change does not cover.
frame_summary: Argues that targeted capital rules in life insurance are routinely outrun by asset innovation, so a rule aimed at one exposure tends to relocate the exposure rather than remove it.
verbatim_quote: people feared a major crackdown in CLOs and so they created other forms of oftentimes similar structured securities to invest in
verbatim_list: The National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) spent four years developing revised risk-based capital (RBC) factors for CLO investments before voting to adopt them on June 23. The new rules, effective for year-end 2026 RBC filings, are designed to protect insurers against losses on approximately US$314 billion of CLO exposure.
notes: Counter-argument evidence: the CLO precedent for exposure re-forming outside a new rule's perimeter. Quote confirmed by hand against the live page during the 17/08/2026 WebFetch: Aaron Sarfatti told the Journal that "people feared a major crackdown in CLOs and so they created other forms of oftentimes similar structured securities to invest in."
